newsitem.title: UK: UK fund calls for Kenwood merger.
newsitem.headline: UK fund calls for Kenwood merger.

text.p: British fund managers on Tuesday called on the directors of household appliance group Kenwood Appliances Plc to consider merging with a bigger group to enhance shareholder value.
Active Value Advisors (AVA), which owns nine percent of the Kenwood, said first-half results published on Tuesday showed management failed "to deliver value to shareholders."
"While Kenwood remains a company with enormous potential, these are weak results from a weak management team, which remains essentially unchanged," AVA spokesman Julian Treger said in a statement.
"Kenwood needs to be part of a larger group which will run the business more efficiently and reduce costs. We believe the directors must begin exploring this option now."
Treger's comments come after Kenwood reported first-half pre-tax profits more than halved to 3.3 million stg from 7.4 million in the same period a year ago.
On Monday, the Financial Times newspaper said household appliances group Pifco Holdings Plc was interested in a merger with Kenwood. On Tuesday, Kenwood said it had not received any formal offers.
Chief executive Tim Beech told Reuters in a telephone interview after the company announced its results that it was unreasonable for AVA to target Kenwood's management team as most were new.

On December 16, Kenwood faces an extraordinary general meeting requisitioned by rebel shareholders who have put a resolution the directors be required to hold discussions with third parties aimed at soliciting a bid for the company.
